shell.nav.tools.note: The rail's accessible name. The product is one panel inside a host app and has no concept of switching between sibling tools, so it has no word for the set. `longtermmemorynavigation.workspacePanes` names the panes INSIDE the memory tool, one level down from this.

shell.tool.presets.note: The prompt-preset tool's rail label. The catalog talks about presets only in possessive phrases bound to the memory block ('Open Prompt Preset Sections', promptBlockPlacement*) and has no bare plural noun for the collection this tool edits.

shell.tool.memory.note: Mirrors the catalog's bare noun, which is lowercase because upstream renders it mid-sentence. Safe here because `.rail-label` uppercases (styles/shell.css); if this label is ever reused in sentence case, coin instead of restyling.

shell.conn.offlineTitle.note: The browser itself is offline. The product runs in-page against a local host and never speaks about the network dropping; its whole error vocabulary is about a request failing, not about there being no link to try.

shell.conn.offlineBody.text: you can read what's already loaded; edits can't be saved until you're back.
shell.conn.offlineBody.note: Says which half of the console still works while offline. The catalog has no degraded-but-usable state at all — upstream failures are terminal per action ('errors.interfaceStopped'), never a mode the user keeps working in.

shell.conn.engineTitle.note: 'Engine' is the product's own noun (longtermmemorydetail.underTheHoodFingerprints, promptBlockPlacementFallback: 'Marinara Engine'), but upstream is co-located with it and so has no string for it being unreachable.

shell.conn.engineBody.text: the engine may be asleep. Your unsaved edits are kept.
shell.conn.engineBody.note: Names the actual cause here — the engine is hosted in Termux over Tailscale and sleeps — and promises drafts survive it. Both facts are deployment-specific and cannot exist upstream.

shell.conn.retry.note: Was 'Retry now'. The banner already supplies the 'now', and the catalog's own retry affordance is the bare verb; the extra word was a coinage buying nothing.

shell.palette.title.note: The dialog's accessible name. The catalog has no occurrence of 'palette' or 'command' in any key or value: the product has no global command surface, so every string in this dialog's chrome is necessarily ours.

shell.palette.searchLabel.note: The input's accessible name, in the catalog's own 'Search {nouns}' shape (searchMemories, searchChats, searchStatuses). The noun is a command, which the product does not have.

shell.palette.placeholder.note: The visible placeholder, naming what the fuzzy index actually spans. Shaped after sourcesworkspace.searchEveryAvailableCharacterLorebookChatAndBranch; the nouns are console nouns, so the sentence cannot be borrowed.

shell.palette.empty.note: The catalog's empty-search family is per noun and always terminal ('No matching chats.', noScopeTargets, noSubjectTargets). It has no generic form, and the palette searches four kinds at once so no single one of them fits.

shell.palette.hintMove.note: Key-hint footer: a key glyph welded to its verb. The verbs exist upstream as button labels (sourceoperation.move) but a glyph-plus-verb hint is a form the product has no instance of, and splitting it would put a bare capitalized 'Move' in a lowercase footer.

shell.palette.hintOpen.note: Key-hint footer, same form as hintMove. The catalog's 'open' is always transitive and bound to an object (openReviewQueue, openChatSources); there is no bare verb to point at.

shell.palette.hintClose.note: Key-hint footer, same form as hintMove. memoryvault.close is the bare verb but capitalized as a button label, and the hint reads as one token with its key name.

shell.palette.groupNavigate.note: Palette result group. The product has one navigation surface and never labels a group of destinations, because it has no list that mixes destinations with actions the way a palette does.

shell.palette.groupActions.note: Palette result group, the counterpart to groupNavigate. The catalog names individual actions everywhere and the category nowhere.

shell.palette.groupEntries.note: Palette result group for lorebook entries. The catalog knows a lorebook only as a SOURCE to import from (sourcesworkspace.lorebooks) and never reaches inside one, so it has no word for the things in it.

shell.palette.goLorebooks.note: Palette navigation command, in the catalog's own 'Go to {destination}' shape (longtermmemorydetail.goToSavedMemories). The destination is a console tool, which upstream has no equivalent of.

shell.palette.goPresets.note: Palette navigation command; same shape and same reason as goLorebooks. Written out rather than interpolated so the tool name reads in title case here while the rail uppercases it.

shell.palette.goMemory.note: Palette navigation command; same shape and same reason as goLorebooks. Title case is deliberate — the mirrored rail label is lowercase and only looks right under the rail's uppercase transform.

shell.palette.density.note: Palette action for the console's row-density preference. Density is a console-only affordance introduced for one-handed phone use; the product ships a single fixed density and has no vocabulary for it.

shell.hotkeys.title.note: The cheat sheet's heading and its dialog's accessible name. The product binds no keys at all, so nothing in this dialog can trace upstream.

shell.hotkeys.palette.text: Command palette — tools, books, entries, actions
shell.hotkeys.palette.note: Cheat-sheet description of ⌘K. Names the same four kinds as the palette placeholder so the two agree; see shell.palette.title for why no part of this traces.

shell.hotkeys.go.note: Cheat-sheet description of the `g` prefix. Collapses the three goTo commands into one row, matching how the binding is actually held in the hand.

shell.hotkeys.move.note: Cheat-sheet description of j/k and the arrows. Focus movement is a keyboard concept the product has no bindings for and therefore no words about.

shell.hotkeys.open.note: Cheat-sheet description of Enter/o. 'Row' is the console's list unit; the catalog's open verbs are all bound to named panels, never to whatever is focused.

shell.hotkeys.close.note: Cheat-sheet description of Escape, which is overloaded: it closes an overlay if one is open and otherwise navigates back. The slash is the honest description of one key with two jobs.

shell.hotkeys.cheat.note: Cheat-sheet description of `?`, the row that names the dialog it sits in. Self-referential by design so the binding is discoverable from inside.

shell.toast.dismiss.note: Accessible name of a toast's × . The catalog has the verb only bound to an object (reviewqueue.dismissReport, dismissing) and never bare; a toast has no object to name, it is the notice itself.

shell.api.noConnection.text: No connection to the console server
shell.api.noConnection.note: Thrown when fetch rejects, i.e. the browser never reached the console's own node server — one hop nearer than shell.conn.engineTitle. The product has no server of its own between the UI and the engine, so it cannot have this failure.

shell.api.restorePointFailed.text: Restore point FAILED — this write proceeded without a backup. Check the server log.
shell.api.restorePointFailed.note: Raised when the server reports x-ltm-restore-point: failed. The catalog's backup strings all report success after the fact (memoryBackupExported, appliedIdentityRepairs '…A backup was created.') and it has nothing for a write that went ahead unprotected.

shell.wire.mismatch.text: The reply to {{context}} did not match what this console expects, so this screen has nothing to show. Check the browser console.
shell.wire.mismatch.note: Raised when a whole response fails its schema. Shares its wording with shell.wire.dropped, the same failure one record at a time. The product is compiled against its own engine and cannot be out of step with it, so it has no string for the two halves disagreeing; its nearest words (longtermmemorydetail.vaultCorrupt, memorysettings.quarantineMalformedNotes) blame stored data rather than the wire.

shell.wire.dropped.one: 1 record in {{context}} did not match what this console expects and was left out. Check the browser console.
shell.wire.dropped.other: {{count}} records in {{context}} did not match what this console expects and were left out. Check the browser console.
shell.wire.dropped.note: Raised when elements of a list fail their schema and the rest still render, so the reader is told the list is short before they notice something missing. Upstream quarantines malformed notes on the server and reports a count afterwards (memorysettings.resultNoMalformedNotes); nothing there describes a client declining to display them.

shell.wire.writeMismatch.text: Your change was made, but the engine's reply to {{context}} is in a shape this console does not recognise. Reload before editing again. Check the browser console.
shell.wire.writeMismatch.note: Raised when a write succeeds and its response fails its schema, which is the one case where the screen and the engine disagree about a change the person has already been told about. Upstream has no string for it: the product is compiled against its own engine, and its write failures (errors.interfaceStopped, longtermmemorydetail.vaultCorrupt) are all about the write not happening rather than about it happening unreadably.

shell.wire.notAList.note: The single issue line recorded when a route that returns a collection returned something else. Reads as a schema issue beside valibot's own, not as a sentence to a person, and the catalog has no vocabulary at that level.
